reasons: overtone: KILL feasibility — reliably tuned, distinguishable resonant pitch from FDM-printed cantilever tines across 30 shells is an unproven acoustic-engineering bet, and the underlying turn structure (must-play-higher-or-take-pile, challenge-and-penalty) is the same one a numbered card already delivers; sound is a delivery wrapper on a classic President/Perudo skeleton. penumbra: KILL feasibility — the game leans on a player's own phone flashlight as a load-bearing component (not in the box, not printed), and 'claim proof by lift' on a soft-edged shadow is an adjudication call, not a measurement, which invites table disputes. snare: KILL collision — ideator's own nearest_known names Sprouts, and Sprouts already is the mechanism (a closing cycle traps a token/spot); swapping pencil lines for snap-links is delivery, not a new mechanism. yield: KILL feasibility — graded internal lattice stiffness that is invisible from above and different in every copy, then adjudicated by a 4mm go/no-go gauge, asks desktop FDM for mm-precision, copy-to-copy-varied sag reproducibility that is not a realistic manufacturing/QA target. crank: KEEP — the compound print-in-place planetary gear with a captive carrier is the cleanest 'why molding breaks' of the five (no parting line, no assembly, unmoldable by definition), the shared-crank resolution genuinely cannot be faked by a cardboard lookup chart once the mesh graph branches, and 'three clicks moves the whole table including the parts you regret' is a real spike-of-love hook squarely on-arm for makers who'll recognize a planetary hub.
